titleEn: Autonomous field robots move into dairy farming
titleZh: 自主田间机器人进入奶牛养殖业
summaryZh: 荷兰奶农Joram Hofman在自家高度自动化的奶牛场测试AgXeed W4自主机器人，用于割草、摊晒和搂草。该机器人通过GPS和Isobus系统与现有设备协同工作，旨在减少人工操作，提高效率。测试由NPPL+R、Agxeed和经销商Weevers-Nieuwstad合作进行，WUR研究员参与评估。文章探讨了自主机器人在草地作业中的应用潜力，以及如何通过传感器改造现有农机以适应机器人作业。
featuredReason: 本文展示了自主田间机器人在奶牛饲草生产中的实际应用案例，结合了高度自动化的奶牛场管理，为智慧畜牧领域的从业者提供了宝贵的实践经验和未来技术方向。

Photos: Koos Groenewold Joram Hofman is testing the Agxeed W4 wheeled robot over a longer period in cooperation with NPPL+R, manufacturer Agxeed and dealer Weevers Nieuwstad. Photos: Koos Groenewold Autonomous field robots are often associated with arable farming, but they may also offer new opportunities for dairy producers. Dutch dairy farmer Joram Hofman is testing an AgXeed W4 autonomous robot for mowing, tedding and raking grass. Future Farming visited the farm to see how the machine fits into an already highly automated dairy operation and what role autonomous field work could play in forage production. Whilst we take a walk around the farm, it soon becomes clear that the dairy farm is highly mechanised and, above all, highly automated. Several autonomous systems can be found in the somewhat old-looking sheds. At the front are 2 Lely A5 milking robots and at the rear of the shed there is a Trioliet feed kitchen. 2 Lely manure robots make their rounds on the slatted floors and all tractors are equipped with GPS and Isobus systems. And there is now also a new robot in the yard, the Agxeed W4, which the livestock farmer will test in cooperation with the Dutch NPPL+R. Hofman & Van der Laan in Lytsewierrum (Frl.) 53 hectaresof grassland 85 dairy cows 9,500 kgmilkcow 4.40% fat 3.70% protein 6 robots !Image 7: Joram Hofman (41) runs the dairy farm and is in a partnership with his father and his girlfriend. In addition, he also sells security cameras under the name Stalzicht and trades in second-hand John Deere GPS systems. Joram Hofman (41) runs the dairy farm and is in a partnership with his father and his girlfriend. In addition, he also sells security cameras under the name Stalzicht and trades in second-hand John Deere GPS systems. Small-scale and highly autonomous Maatschap Hofman & Van der Laan is based in Lytsewierrum (Frl.). Hofman runs it together with his girlfriend and father, and also sells surveillance cameras specifically for agriculture under the name Stalzicht. The entrepreneur also trades in second-hand GPS systems from John Deere. “The farm is not big enough for 3 people, but with the 2 additional activities we are busy enough overall,” Hofman says. The farm has 85 dairy cows, 53 hectares of grassland and milk production of around 9,500 kg of milk per cow. In addition, the dairy farmer carries out all field work himself, except for spreading slurry. A robot tractor of more than 200 hp does not suit our farm management and our land “We bought the autonomous systems, both the milking robots and the feeding robot, to replace my father’s work,” Hofman jokes. “My father is now 70 and wants to scale back a little. The robots mean he can take things easier.” Hofman also uses the data from the robots to optimise his farm management. “I have created an AI model that calculates the ration for the cows for me using the data I receive from the robots and the dairy,” Hofman explains. With the use of this system and the introduction of the feeding robot, Hofman has started feeding more efficiently. “I do not think milk yield has increased because of the feeding robot, but I am now using feed more efficiently,” the dairy farmer concludes. He also notices that there is much more calm in the shed. The only machines that still come onto the feed passage are the electrically driven feeding robot and mini loader, neither of which makes much noise. The cows have now become so used to that calm that, should a tractor drive along the feed passage, the cows and especially the youngstock are startled badly by the noise. !Image 8 Raking and baling in 1 pass When we look at the machines, 1 detail immediately stands out. 2 of the 3 tractors do not have a cab. “That is nice, is it not,” Hofman says. Hofman only works in the field when the weather is good, and then an open tractor is much more enjoyable to work with, the livestock farmer says. The second thing that stands out in the machinery shed is the rake on the front linkage of the John Deere. “My father always did the raking, but he is doing less of that now too,” Hofman says. To avoid losing efficiency, Hofman wanted to rake and bale in 1 pass. Hofman has had the combination since the 5th cut last year and is pleased with it. “Raking the headland is a bit awkward, so if it works out my father still does that with the normal rake. I can now rake using GPS without the bales being poorly filled as a result,” Hofman concludes. The rake is set up precisely for the baler, making the swath so wide that Hofman no longer has to weave with the baler to get a well-filled bale. !Image 9: Before the robot can start mowing, the combination is made autonomy-ready. The robot drives in reverse, so the bumper is moved to the rear of the robot. For this, the mechanisation company is making a stand on the mower in which the mechanic hangs the bumper. Before the robot can start mowing, the combination is made autonomy-ready. The robot drives in reverse, so the bumper is moved to the rear of the robot. For this, the mechanisation company is making a stand on the mower in which the mechanic hangs the bumper. The new robot on the farm Alongside all the machinery and robots, Hofman has had a new robot on the yard since this week: the Agxeed W4. Hofman is testing this 4-wheel robot for more than a month in cooperation with NPPL+R and Agxeed. “I was also interested in the system from iQuus, but the tractor we could test had more than 200 hp and that does not suit our farm management and our land,” Hofman says. When the dairy farmer got talking to Agxeed during the NPPL participants’ day, the idea arose to test the 75 hp wheeled robot. I am very curious to see how the robot fits within the machinery fleet and how much has to be adapted Mainly mowing The robot will mainly do the mowing work for the livestock farmer. After the first cut, Hofman always mows a small area at a time to stay in line with the cows’ grazing. For him, the test will be successful if he can put the robot in the field and it carries out the mowing neatly. “I am quite interested in the possibilities of a robot, but at our farm scale it is not viable to buy an Agxeed. This is a good way to become familiar with the technology,” Hofman says. In addition to mowing, the dairy farmer also wants to ted and rake with the robot. He also sees the possibility of automating pasture harrowing and fertiliser spreading. “My spreader spreads using GPS and Isobus on the basis of task maps. Since the robot has an Isobus connection, it should work, but that will still be a small challenge.” !Image 10: To make the mower autonomy-ready, a sensor has been fitted to the mower’s PTO shaft. If the PTO now stops rotating, the robot also stops. To ensure a good signal, rust is removed from the PTO shaft. Photo: Lucas van de Weijer To make the mower autonomy-ready, a sensor has been fitted to the mower’s PTO shaft. If the PTO now stops rotating, the robot also stops. To ensure a good signal, rust is removed from the PTO shaft. Photo: Lucas van de Weijer In addition to being technically able to carry out the work, the work itself also has to go well. “I now have to start thinking about everything that could go wrong and how that can be detected with sensors,” Hofman says thoughtfully. Together with dealer Weevers-Nieuwstad from Lelystad and researchers from WUR, the livestock farmer is looking at which sensors and modifications are needed on the machinery to allow the robot to do its work safely and reliably. !Image 11: Working with autonomous systems is not new for Joram Hofman. A Trioliet feeding robot, 2 Lely milking robots and 2 Lely feeding robots are operating on his farm, and all tractors are equipped with GPS and Isobus systems. Working with autonomous systems is not new for Joram Hofman. A Trioliet feeding robot, 2 Lely milking robots and 2 Lely feeding robots are operating on his farm, and all tractors are equipped with GPS and Isobus systems. “This is the first time NPPL has tested an Agxeed robot in grassland cultivation and harvesting, so it is a bit of pioneering,” says WUR researcher Koen van Boheemen. “I hope the robot’s performance comes close to that of a human driver. Should something unusual happen, it remains to be seen whether it is the robot’s fault. translationZh:
自主田间机器人通常与耕地农业联系在一起，但它们也可能为奶农带来新的机遇。荷兰奶农Joram Hofman正在测试一台AgXeed W4自主机器人，用于割草、摊晒和搂草。Future Farming走访了该农场，了解这台机器如何融入一个已经高度自动化的奶牛场，以及自主田间作业在饲草生产中能发挥什么作用。

我们在农场里走了一圈，很快就发现这个奶牛场高度机械化，而且最重要的是高度自动化。在略显陈旧的棚舍里，可以看到几套自主系统。前面是两台Lely A5挤奶机器人，棚舍后面是一套Trioliet饲喂厨房。两台Lely清粪机器人在漏缝地板上巡回，所有拖拉机都配备了GPS和Isobus系统。现在院子里又多了一台新机器人——Agxeed W4，这位奶农将与荷兰NPPL+R合作进行测试。

**小而高度自主**

Maatschap Hofman & Van der Laan农场位于Lytsewierrum（弗里斯兰省）。Hofman与女友和父亲共同经营，同时还以Stalzicht品牌销售专用于农业的监控摄像头，并二手交易约翰迪尔GPS系统。Hofman说：“这个农场规模不足以养活三个人，但加上这两项副业，我们总体上很忙。”农场有85头奶牛，53公顷草地，每头牛年产奶量约9500公斤。此外，除撒粪浆外，所有田间作业都由他自己完成。

“我们购买这些自主系统，无论是挤奶机器人还是饲喂机器人，都是为了替代我父亲的工作，”Hofman开玩笑说。“我父亲现在70岁了，想稍微轻松一点。机器人让他能更省力。”Hofman还利用机器人数据优化农场管理。“我创建了一个AI模型，利用机器人和乳品厂的数据为我计算奶牛日粮，”Hofman解释道。通过这套系统和饲喂机器人的引入，Hofman的饲喂效率提高了。“我不认为挤奶量因为饲喂机器人而增加，但我现在饲料利用更高效了，”奶农总结道。他还注意到棚舍里安静了许多。现在只有电动饲喂机器人和小型装载机在饲喂通道上行驶，噪音都不大。奶牛已经习惯了这种安静，以至于如果有拖拉机驶过饲喂通道，奶牛尤其是青年牛会被噪音吓一大跳。

**搂草和打捆一次完成**

我们看机器时，一个细节立刻引起注意。三台拖拉机中有两台没有驾驶室。“这很好，不是吗？”Hofman说。Hofman只在天气好时下地干活，那时开放式拖拉机更让人愉快，这位奶农说。机库里第二个引人注目的是约翰迪尔前悬挂上的搂草机。“以前搂草总是我父亲做，但他现在也做得少了，”Hofman说。为了避免效率损失，Hofman想一次性完成搂草和打捆。从去年第五茬草开始，他就用上了这套组合，并且很满意。“地头搂草有点麻烦，所以如果可能的话，我父亲还是用普通搂草机做。我现在可以用GPS搂草，而且草捆不会因此填充不好，”Hofman总结道。搂草机精确对准打捆机，草条宽度合适，Hofman不再需要为了填满草捆而让打捆机走“之”字形。

**农场上的新机器人**

除了所有机器和机器人，Hofman这周院子里还多了一台新机器人：Agxeed W4。Hofman将这台四轮机器人测试一个多月，合作方包括NPPL+R和Agxeed。“我也对iQuus的系统感兴趣，但我们可以测试的拖拉机超过200马力，不适合我们的农场管理和土地，”Hofman说。当这位奶农在NPPL参与者日与Agxeed交谈时，产生了测试这台75马力轮式机器人的想法。

**主要是割草**

这台机器人将主要为奶农做割草工作。头茬草之后，Hofman总是小块地割草，以配合奶牛放牧。对他来说，如果能把机器人放到地里，它能整齐地完成割草，测试就算成功。“我对机器人的可能性很感兴趣，但以我们农场的规模，买一台Agxeed并不划算。这是了解这项技术的好方法，”Hofman说。除了割草，这位奶农还想用机器人摊晒和搂草。他还看到了自动化草地耙平和施肥的可能性。“我的施肥机基于任务地图通过GPS和Isobus工作。既然机器人有Isobus接口，应该能行，但那仍会是个小挑战。”

除了技术上能完成工作，工作本身也必须做好。“我现在必须开始考虑所有可能出错的地方，以及如何用传感器检测到这些，”Hofman若有所思地说。他与来自Lelystad的经销商Weevers-Nieuwstad以及WUR的研究人员一起，研究需要哪些传感器和改装，才能让机器人安全可靠地完成工作。

“这是NPPL第一次在草地种植和收获中测试Agxeed机器人，所以有点开拓性质，”WUR研究员Koen van Boheemen说。“我希望机器人的性能接近人类驾驶员。如果发生异常情况，还要看是否是机器人的问题。田间的变异、割草机或其他由机器人驱动的机器也可能导致问题。”对Van Boheemen来说，如果奶农满意，测试就算成功。“我很想知道机器人如何融入现有机械队伍，以及为了可靠地与机器人配合，机器需要做多少调整。”
